name: Gale and still point
era_span: The Imperial Age: Ravenn's card states it and names no era inside it; the other four cards state no era. All three events fall in the Imperial Age with no year and no era inside it named; the caldera belt event comes after the Accord chartered the arc.

members.line: Eldest of the Kazuren siblings and current clan head, raised from childhood at the Quiet Shrine; Clan Head, Duelist and Monastic Sentinel of the Kazuren line, in her early thirties. She "has not stopped watching her younger siblings since" she took the clan, "convinced a major Wellspring fracture will eventually call them together"; a room settles when she enters it, sound dulls near her, and her breathing sets the room's tempo. She carries the Twin Vows. Nobody knows why the previous head stepped down, "and whether Sairin already knows and is only waiting for her siblings to ask."

The middle Kazuren sibling, in his late twenties, "Eastern Human; realm unstated"; formerly of the Dreamfold Monastery, which he "left after a schism only he understood" ("Left, not exiled"), now an unaffiliated mediator and reality-reader, "the man who prevents the disaster before it starts". His Lantern Calm weakens hostile intent; he carries the Veilshade Umbrella, its blade rarely drawn; he does not explain the dream-work to anyone.

"Human, Kingdom of Veyran descent, with an atavistic wind-aspect mutation"; former disciple of the Gale Monastery and its only survivor, an unaffiliated wanderer of the Imperial Age. His damaged left eye reads air currents, his Wind-Shear Line cuts in a straight line and is paid for in torn tendon and "days of stillness", and his exile is total. Frontier settlements know him as the reason bandit routes "sometimes simply stop". "Calm is not peace. Calm is restraint."

Freed gladiator of Kael'Nir's arena, "of Veyran gale-blood", now a wandering anti-slavery mercenary hunting traffickers along the trade routes and refusing every Guild Accord recruitment offer. The Chainpit Uprising freed forty-three and "cost him whatever the arena still had a claim on"; he still wears the broken shackles. He wants the story told. Nobody knows whether his Feral Tempest State is gale-blood or the arena's training.

"Varrisak and human"; "Once a wind-priest of Kael'Nir's temple choir", transcended at the Verdant Ascension, "refused sainthood, and chose to wander as a Harmony Arbiter for the Guild Accord", in the Arbitration Division. Listeners mirror his rhythm; his Tranquil Spiral, a circle of sound, "neutralises rage"; Lung Fracture turns his breath into song. "He speaks as if everything already happened and never reveals how he knows". "His name lingers in monastic hymns."

events.name: The road out of Kael'Nir
events.when: The Imperial Age, the era inside it unstated. The Chainpit Uprising was just done: Karu had broken the forty-three free, and it had cost him whatever the arena still had a claim on. Iryen was still a wind-priest of the temple choir. The Verdant Ascension and his refusal of sainthood were still ahead of him.
events.where: Kael'Nir, on the forest road out of it, below the temple. Tsukihana Reimei's card sets "the border province of Kael'Nir forests" in Eresse, in the New World (WORLD §3; c13). No page places the arena, the temple or the road, and this record places them no nearer than her card does.
events.what: Karu brought the freed out of the arena in the dark. Some were hurt. Others could barely keep their feet. The road out ran through the forest below the temple, and Iryen came down to it from the temple steps. He did not ask who they were. He looked at the broken shackles on Karu's wrists, and then he went to the head of the column. He sang under his breath as he walked. The column fell into his pace, slow and even, and the ones who had been stumbling kept up. Karu walked at the rear with the chains. Where the trees thinned at the forest's edge, Iryen stopped. Karu told him the story of the pit, all of it, as he tells it to anyone who will hear it. Iryen heard him out and said he knew it already. He did not say how. He turned back up the road to the temple before it was light, and the column went on without him. Took: Karu: the forty-three brought out of Kael'Nir at a wind-priest's pace; a man from the temple who heard the whole story and said he had known it. Iryen: a night on the road outside the choir, at the head of people the arena had held. He went back to the temple that morning. He left it later, by the refusal his card records.

events.name: The ford on the Horse Rivers
events.when: The Imperial Age, the era inside it unstated. After the Gale Monastery Collapse, in Ravenn's wandering; after the Chainpit Uprising, while Karu hunted traffickers along the trade routes. After the road out of Kael'Nir, and unordered against the caldera belt.
events.where: A ford on one of the Horse Rivers, in the Southern Grass Sea of the Outer World (WORLD §3 and §5, South; SW, where the Horse Rivers are among the Grass Sea's features), on a grain road through the marcher country. There a farmer "might live beneath a Veyran king" and "travel an Akhazar-recognised road" (D10). The Kingdom of Veyran holds its horse-and-grain country there by treaty (SW). This record places the ford inside no border.
events.what: A string of carts had been taking people off the grain roads, and Karu had followed it south. When he came down to the ford the string had already stopped. The carts stood in the shallows with the teams still in the traces. The drivers were down on the far bank. The ropes on the people in the carts had been cut through, each in one straight line, and a cart's side-board was split the same way. Ravenn sat on the near bank with his breath slowed almost to nothing. He did not get up. The people from the carts backed away from Karu when they saw the chains on his wrists. He stopped where he stood and told them where the chains had come from. When he had finished, they let him near. Some were hurt and could not be moved at once, and Ravenn could not walk. Karu kept camp at the ford. At the fire, through the days that followed, he told Ravenn the story of the Chainpit. Ravenn listened. His scarred left eye kept to the air round Karu's wrists, where the bracers stirred it. Karu felt the pressure change when Ravenn breathed. He asked whether the wind in Ravenn's blood ever took him the way it took Karu. Ravenn said, "Calm is not peace. Calm is restraint." Karu asked him to walk the routes with him. Ravenn refused. On the day he could walk he went off across the grass, away from the road and the settlements. Karu took the people up the road to the nearest village. Took: Ravenn: days of stillness paid for the lines he cut, spent beside a stranger's fire; an offer of company, refused; a man of the same Veyran wind, whose wind goes feral. Karu: a string stopped before he reached it, and its people to see up the road; the Chainpit told once more, to a man who heard it out; a second man of Veyran blood who keeps his wind held. Whether his own state is the blood or the arena stays where his card leaves it.

events.name: The drift in the caldera belt
events.when: The Imperial Age, after the Accord chartered the arc "within living memory" (NW). After Shiran left the Dreamfold Monastery; after Sairin took the clan; after Iryen refused sainthood and took the Arbiter's office. After the road out of Kael'Nir, and unordered against the ford.
events.where: The caldera belt of the Accord-chartered arc in the New World (WORLD §3 and §5, East; NW), where "The Wellsprings here move" (NW, The Ground Itself) and the Arbitration Division "spends a disproportionate share of its calendar on the arc's colonial rights, Wellspring access" (NW, Trade Posture). Two ventures' claims, side by side. This record places neither the Kazuren home, the Quiet Shrine nor the Dreamfold, and names no realm for Shiran.
events.what: The ground under the belt settled in the night, and the Wellspring under one venture's array drifted onto the next claim. The first array went dead. The neighbour's woke. Each venture had a militia, and each militia carried Onceglass charges (NW). The first venture filed with the Accord. Shiran was in the belt before the filing had gone far, and no one on either claim had sent for him. He walked between the two yards with his umbrella closed. He sat with each master in turn, and while he was there no charge was thrown. Sairin came up the road some days after him. She took a place on the slope above the claims, where she could see both yards, and she did not go down. Iryen came with the Accord's filing. He greeted Shiran and spoke of the days before he came as if he had watched every one of them. Shiran did not say how he had known to come. Iryen stood on the drift ground and sang. The tone went out in a circle to the edges of both yards. Inside it the militias put up their charges, and the two masters talked terms, and Iryen sang breath after breath while they talked. Sairin had come down to the circle's edge. Where she stood the tone went dull, and the men nearest her kept her pace. She stepped back out past the edge of the circle, and the tone closed. The masters signed: the neighbour would share the draw with the first venture for as long as the drift held. Iryen's breath came shorter afterward, and more of it was song. Sairin went down the road the next morning, and Shiran did not ask her why she had come. She did not ask him about the Dreamfold. Took: Shiran: days in the belt with no charge thrown, and the quarrel settled by another man's tone; a mediator who knew those days before anyone told him of them; his sister on the slope, and nothing asked on either side. Iryen: a settlement sung breath by breath, and a shorter breath after it; a man who had held the yards before him and would not say how he knew to come; a woman his circle could not take in, who stepped out of it so that it held. Sairin: her brother at his work between two armed yards; a peace she could keep by standing outside it; a Wellspring that moved and did not break.

ties.summary: Both cards make them Kazuren siblings, she the eldest and clan head, he the middle; in the caldera belt she watched him hold two armed yards from the slope, and neither asked the other anything.

Both come out of Kael'Nir by their cards, the arena and the temple choir; after the Chainpit Uprising the wind-priest walked at the head of the forty-three to the forest's edge and heard Karu's story in full.
Both carry the Veyran wind by their cards; at the Horse Rivers ford Karu found the string Ravenn had stopped, kept camp beside him through his days of stillness, and was refused as a companion.
Two mediators at one quarrel in the caldera belt: Shiran held the yards before anyone sent for him, Iryen settled them with a tone, and neither said how he knew what he knew.
The Still Point stood at the edge of the Serene Gale's circle, dulled his tone where she stood, and stepped out of it so that it held.

outward.wants: the youngest Kazuren sibling. Her card's siblings are "Younger", in the plural, and Shiran's card makes him the middle, so at least one more stands below him. No card names them. Beside that, the previous clan head, who "Stepped down voluntarily" and has no name or card.

someone of the Dreamfold Monastery who stayed after the schism. No card names one. Failing that, a fellow dream-worker of Oneirion: Liorien Nael-Teth (c37), whose Oneirion runs a "dream-journaling discipline", or Aeldoris Vanthryx (c28), who hunts "the fractures people hide inside".

a keeper or rider of House Dovaryn, whose wyverns fly over the Southern Grass Sea (D10, "watch Dovaryn Wyverns overhead"). His card records a rogue wyvern put down at the Whisperwind Pass. No page says whose it was.

a free blade on the same roads. c13 already names Karu as the outward tie for Azhura Vyren, "a free blade on the same roads who refuses the Accord she serves". Failing her, the Guild Accord officer who has carried its recruitment offers and been refused.

Tsukihana Reimei (c13), of "the border province of Kael'Nir forests", whose reflection rites "drew notice from the Arbitration Division" before Enforcement took her. Her mentor, High Arbiter Saen (her card, unattested), is the one Arbitration name any card gives near Kael'Nir.

card_contradictions: Each Kazuren card says the other sibling is unnamed. Sairin's card: "The Kazuren siblings · Younger, unnamed on the card." (IX). Shiran's card: "Middle sibling of the Kazuren family (other siblings unnamed in the source; not detailed elsewhere)" (I). Sairin's card names the eldest, and Shiran's card is a younger sibling carded.

Whether the Kazuren Clan is attested. The Fractured Dawn lists "the Kazuren Clan" among names that "returned no hits against the wiki and are unattested in current canon" (head note), against the two Kazuren cards. Its "the Kazuren Clan reads the Bleed as the Great Spirit War's second coming" sets the clan in the Fractured Era, which ER calls opinion and the count does not hold (WORLD §1); neither Kazuren card gives the clan an era.

The Regency. Shiran's card: "Unnamed disputing parties across the Regency" (IX). `RULINGS.md`, 2026-09-12: "Mireya is struck", with "no replacement place named", and its strike "left six spots leaning on an unnamed place, for Isaac to name if he wants", among them "Shiran Kazuren's realm ("unstated")". The one regency on the Table pages is "The Sunroot Regency under Ovaeren" in the New World (`Fronts, as clocks.md`).

Whether Veyran is attested. Aeldoris Vanthryx's card: "Veyran is unattested; see the migration note." The Southern Pan page: "The Kingdom of Veyran, a horse-and-grain monarchy". Ravenn's card: "Kingdom of Veyran descent". c19 and c28 record the same disagreement.

Glory without its Catalyst, on one card. Sairin's card: "Catalyst Event · Stage VI, Glory." and her stat line sits at that Stage (I, IV), while the same card says "The card gives no fracture yet to answer, only the conviction that one is coming. The Threshold is not behind her. She priced it in advance." (I). Nothing here supplies the event.
